help: AI uses `let _ = ...` to silence unused_must_use warnings. The Result error is now invisible. Either handle it (`?`, match, or explicit ignore with `// IGNORED:` comment) or fix the issue.

message: `pub fn -> Result<T, Box<dyn Error>>` in library code — use typed errors.
help: Library APIs should expose typed errors (define an error enum + thiserror). `Box<dyn Error>` works for binaries but defeats caller-side error handling. Effective Rust Item 4.

message: `defer` inside a for/range loop — leaks N-1 resources until function returns.
help: `defer X.Close()` fires at function exit, NOT loop iteration. AI uses defer-in-loop reflexively and leaks file descriptors / connections. Extract the loop body to a function with its own defer, or close explicitly. gocritic deferInLoop.

message: `defer X.Close()` placed before the `if err != nil` check — nil-deref panic on error.
help: `resp, err := http.Get(url); defer resp.Body.Close(); if err != nil { return }` — if Get returns an error, resp is nil and the deferred Close panics. Check err FIRST, then defer.

message: HTTP request body not closed — connection leak.
help: `http.Get`/`Post`/`Do` returns a `*Response` whose `Body` must be Closed. Otherwise the connection isn't returned to the pool. `defer resp.Body.Close()` after err check. golangci-lint bodyclose.

message: `fmt.Errorf("...: %v", err)` breaks the error chain — use %w to wrap.
help: Go 1.13+ supports error wrapping with `%w`. `%v` formats the error as text but `errors.Is`/`errors.As` can't traverse the chain. Replace `%v` with `%w`. golangci-lint errorlint.

AI forgets to thread `ctx` through function params; reaches for `Background()`. Receivers of work should accept `ctx context.Context` and propagate it — breaking the chain breaks cancellation. golangci-lint contextcheck.

Array methods like forEach/map/filter don't await async callbacks — they discard the Promise. Use `for...of` for sequential or `Promise.all(arr.map(...))` for parallel. typescript-eslint no-misused-promises.
`if (userExists(id))` evaluates the Promise, which is truthy. The function never reaches the false branch. Use `if (await userExists(id))`. typescript-eslint no-misused-promises (checksConditionals).

message: `Promise<any>` return type — AI hedge when uncertain of response shape.
help: Type-narrow with zod/valibot or return `Promise<unknown>` and force callers to narrow. `Promise<any>` disables type-checking through the rest of the call chain.

message: `req.body as SomeType` — type assertion on untrusted input without runtime validation.
help: AI casts request bodies / JSON responses to TS types without validating shape at runtime. Use zod/valibot/arktype: `SignupReq.parse(req.body)`. Auto-suppressed if file imports zod/valibot/arktype/yup/joi.

message: `onClick={handler(arg)}` invokes at render — every render fires the handler.
help: `<button onClick={deleteItem(id)}>` calls deleteItem on every render. Use `onClick={() => deleteItem(id)}` or `onClick={handler}` (no parens) for a no-arg handler.
`useState([])` infers `never[]`; `useState<any>` disables type-checking. Provide a type parameter: `useState<Item[]>([])`.

message: Hook call inside a conditional block — rules-of-hooks violation.
help: React hooks must be called at the top level of a component, never inside if/for/while or after early returns. Lift the hook to the top and condition the value, not the call. eslint-plugin-react-hooks/rules-of-hooks.

message: `async function` in a file with `"use client"` — invalid Next.js client component.
help: Async functions can't be client components in Next.js app router. Move data fetching to a parent server component or use the `use()` hook. @next/next/no-async-client-component.

message: useEffect responding to a flag — should be in the event handler.
help: `useEffect(() => { if (submitted) fetch(...) }, [submitted])` should be in the form's onSubmit. react.dev 'You Might Not Need an Effect'.

message: Client API (useState/useEffect/onClick) used without `"use client"` directive in app/ directory.
help: Next.js app router needs `"use client"` at the top of files that use client-only APIs. Add it as the first line.
